title: The Five Most Ignorant People in Agra (HI)
summary: Akbar orders Birbal to find the five most foolish men in the empire. Birbal brings three absurd strangers and names the remaining two with brilliant wit. [HI]
full_text:
Frustrated by endless bureaucratic blunders in his administration, Emperor Akbar sighed to Birbal: 'Our capital is overflowing with ignorance! Birbal, I give you three days to find and bring before my throne the five greatest fools in Agra!'

Birbal departed. On the third day, he returned to the palace with three men.

The first man was riding a donkey while carrying a heavy bundle of firewood upon his own head. When Akbar asked why, the man replied: 'Sire, my poor donkey is old! If I put the wood on his back, it would crush him, so I carry it on my own head to spare the beast!'

The second man was sitting on the branch of a tall banyan tree, sawing off the very same branch he was sitting on, directly between himself and the trunk!

The third man was standing in the middle of a flooded river, holding a cup of river water, screaming for someone to bring him a drink because he was dying of thirst!

Akbar laughed heartily at the three fools, then turned to Birbal: 'These three are indeed magnificent fools. But I commanded you to bring five! Where are the other two?'

Birbal folded his hands and looked at Akbar with serene respect:

'Sire, the fourth fool is myself—who spent three precious days neglecting vital governance and the welfare of the people to hunt down harmless fools!

'And with deepest humility, Your Majesty, the fifth fool is Your Imperial Majesty—who commissioned a wise minister to waste royal time and treasury on such a nonsensical quest instead of attending to the affairs of state!'

The courtiers held their breath in terror at Birbal's audacity. But Akbar stared for a moment, then threw his head back and roared with laughter:

'You speak the absolute truth, Birbal! He who hunts for fools is the greatest fool of all!' Akbar rewarded Birbal with gold for his fearless honesty.
